channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump Orders Contractors to Get Approval for Congress Queries
item.description: President Donald Trump issued an executive order requiring federal contractors to notify the White House of any congressional requests for their communications, as the White House prepares for inquiries when Democrats take over Congress in the new year.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Gray

item.title: Brazil’s Jair Bolsonaro Admitted to ICU With Obstruction
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro was admitted to an intensive care unit with an acute intestinal obstruction after being hospitalized with severe abdominal pain, according to a statement from the hospital on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Republicans’ Midterm Defeat Corners Vance as 2028 Field Widens
item.description: A generational defeat in the midterm elections has left Republicans reeling, with little time to regroup and an expanding field of potential candidates vying to be the party’s presidential nominee in 2028.
item.dc:creator: Aidan Williams, Josh Wingrove, Kate Sullivan and Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Mexico Arrests Sinaloa Drug Kingpin on FBI’s Most Wanted List
item.description: Mexican security forces arrested one of the FBI’s 10 most-wanted fugitives, a suspected drug trafficker accused of smuggling narcotics into the US for more than two decades.
item.dc:creator: Maya Averbuch

item.title: Zelenskyy Names Potential Candidates for Ukraine’s US Ambassador Post
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has suggested a number of potential candidates to be the country’s next ambassador the US, a post vacant since August.
item.dc:creator: Kollen Post

item.title: Venezuela’s New Leader Walks a Political Tightrope
item.description: New Yorker staff writer Jon Lee Anderson tells Bloomberg This Weekend that acting Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez is navigating an extraordinary relationship with Washington after the US captured Nicolás Maduro, as she seeks to preserve power while moving away from parts of the country’s socialist legacy. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Anderson discusses Rodríguez’s political evolution, questions surrounding her role in Maduro’s removal and whether Venezuela’s deepening ties with the US can survive a future change in American leadership. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Clean-up of Downed Crimea Bridge to Take Russia Months, Ukraine Says
item.description: Ukraine anticipates that clearing debris from the bridge linking mainland Russia to the Crimean peninsula, damaged in a string of attacks this week, will take Russia a number of months.
item.dc:creator: Kollen Post

item.title: Burnham’s Big Worry Isn’t Brexit or Welfare, It’s Trump and Iran
item.description: In public, Andy Burnham’s recent focus has been on securing better trade terms with the European Union and reforming Britain’s welfare system. In private, the prime minister has been preoccupied by a more global problem: what happens next in the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Switzerland Prolongs Neutrality Soul-Searching With Weapons Vote
item.description: Switzerland is once again debating its longstanding neutrality, extending a dilemma that’s plagued the country since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Levin Stamm and Fabrice Obrist

item.title: Trump Vows To Tax US Companies Building Data Centers Abroad
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Dean Curnutt, founder and CEO of Macro Risk Advisors, says the market selloff could prove “cleansing” by resetting valuations and making room for fresh capital, but warns that the growing overlap between the AI trade and the broader economy could leave markets vulnerable to further downside. Doug Rediker, managing partner at International Capital Strategy, says the market correction is helping “rationalize and normalize” the AI thesis after a period of heavy investment and rising financing risk, calling the pullback both necessary and healthy. New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham says prospective 2028 Democratic presidential contenders are already making their presence felt in the state, naming Mark Kelly, Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Cory Booker among those who have been on the ground. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Historic Market Selloff Deepens After Anthropic IPO
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are ProShares Head of Research and CIO of Active Investments Alessio De Longis, PsiQuantum CEO Victor Peng, Barclays Senior Equity Analyst Brandon Oglenski, Hindlian Advisory Founder & CEO Amanda Hindlian, Charles Schwab Chief Investment Strategist Liz Ann Sonders, Envestnet CIO & EVP of Wealth Solutions Dana D’Auria, T. Rowe Price Portfolio Manager, Science & Tech Equity Tony Wang, Scribe Co-Founder & CEO Jennifer Smith, J&J Snack Foods CEO Dan Fachner, & Trujillo Group Founder Sol Trujillo & Citi Head of Wealth Andy Sieg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gov. Lujan Grisham: 2028 Hopefuls Already Eyeing New Mexico
item.description: New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham says prospective 2028 Democratic presidential contenders are already making their presence felt in the state, naming Mark Kelly, Rahm Emanuel, Pete Buttigieg and Cory Booker among those who have been on the ground. New Mexico is set to vote fourth in the Democratic presidential primary calendar. She also discusses permitting reform and the growing data-center buildout with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sol Trujillo Says Latino Economic Growth Is an Undervalued Investment Opportunity
item.description: Sol Trujillo & Andy Sieg discuss Citi’s partnership with Trujillo to invest in and expand financial access for the Latino population in the United States. They said the opportunity is attractive but has been overlooked because investors have not segmented the data to see its scale. The two speak with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rediker: AI Selloff Is a ‘Healthy’ Correction
item.description: Doug Rediker, managing partner at International Capital Strategy, says the market correction is helping “rationalize and normalize” the AI thesis after a period of heavy investment and rising financing risk, calling the pullback both necessary and healthy. He also says geopolitical uncertainty is becoming increasingly difficult for markets to quantify, but adds that he is “not as upset as some otherwise might be” about the risks. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Plunge After Anthropic IPO, Trump Returns from Asia
item.description: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Managing Partner & Head of CVC Marathon Bruce Richards and BlackRock Chief Investment & Portfolio Strategist Gargi Chaudhrui. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Curnutt: Selloff May Be ‘Cleansing,’ But Risks Remain
item.description: Dean Curnutt, founder and CEO of Macro Risk Advisors, says the market selloff could prove “cleansing” by resetting valuations and making room for fresh capital, but warns that the growing overlap between the AI trade and the broader economy could leave markets vulnerable to further downside. He also sees short-dated Treasuries as a haven if the Federal Reserve is forced to reverse course. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Historic Winner of Texas Oil Regulator Seat Wants Faster Permits
item.description: The first Democrat in 36 years to win a seat on the commission that governs the oil and gas industry in Texas said he plans to work with his Republican colleagues to speed up permitting in the state.
item.dc:creator: David Wethe

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Huang Behavior Complaints
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
About two decades ago, two Nvidia employees complained about how then-Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang treated his staff. Stephen Pettigrew, the first in-house lawyer hired by Nvidia, said he observed Huang regularly verbally abusing and intimidating employees, according to court documents filed in the Superior Court of California. Pettigrew alleged he was fired for raising concerns about the conduct of Nvidia executives, while the company cited performance issues for his termination, according to court documents.
On today’s episode: Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor of Consumer Technology Anna Wong, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Huang Behavior Complaints, Kalshi to Add Stock Trading
item.description: All on the latest episode of "Bloomberg Businessweek Daily." On the show today, Ian King, Bloomberg News US Semiconductor Reporter, Anna Wong, Bloomberg Economics Chief US Economist, Ryan Gould, Bloomberg News Deals Reporter, Mark Gurman, Bloomberg News Managing Editor of Consumer Technology, Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Are the Houthis So Hard for Saudi Arabia to Defeat?
item.description: After four years of relative calm, the war pitting Yemen’s Houthi militia against the country’s internationally recognized government and its backer Saudi Arabia is raging again.
item.dc:creator: Veena Ali-Khan, Paul Wallace and Gerry Doyle
